definition.objective: Calculate computational-basis probabilities from normalized amplitudes.

definition.title: Compare simple promised oracles
definition.objective: Trace phase kickback and predict the two-input-qubit example.
definition.instructions: Known promised oracle: f(x1x0)=0 (constant), identity oracle. Keep the starter preparation/oracle. Add final H gates to q0/q1, then measure q0→c0 and q1→c1. Predict c1c0.
definition.reflection: Read c1c0, the input bits only. Under the Deutsch–Jozsa promise, 00 identifies a constant function; a nonzero input result identifies a balanced one.

definition.title: Amplify |11⟩
definition.objective: Explain a phase oracle followed by diffusion.
definition.instructions: The starter creates equal amplitudes and marks |11⟩ with CZ. Run it to see that phase marking alone leaves equal probabilities. Append one diffusion step, then predict and Run again. Keep the starter intact.
definition.reflection: The oracle changes a phase without changing probabilities. Diffusion converts that phase difference into increased marked-state probability.

definition.title: Trace all four correction branches
definition.instructions: Guided teleportation: keep the protocol scaffold. q0 is the input, q1/q2 share a Bell pair; q0→c0 and q1→c1. Append conditional corrections on Bob q2: X when c1=1 and Z when c0=1, using “Classical registers and conditions” below the gate library. Predict Alice’s c1c0 distribution. Validate checks all four branches and several input states.
definition.reflection: Alice’s c1c0 bits select Bob’s corrections. They do not encode the amplitudes of the input state. Correct recovery requires both classical bits.

definition.title: Compare useful and unhelpful orders
definition.objective: Trace the reduction from factoring to order finding.
definition.instructions: Conceptual exercise; no Shor circuit is executed. For N=15, a=2, enter powers for exponents 1–4, order and the two gcd factors (ascending). Compare a=14: enter its order and gcd(14^(r/2)−1,15), gcd(14^(r/2)+1,15). Fourier samples inform order inference; this arithmetic is classical post-processing.
definition.reflection: This is classical modular arithmetic illustrating the factoring reduction, not a quantum Shor execution.

prediction.prompt: Commit your arithmetic answers, then check your reasoning.

checks.message: Verify modular powers, the least positive order and gcd factors.

rules.message: Verify modular powers, the least positive order and gcd factors.

feedback.summary: Order finding and classical factor extraction completed.
feedback.explanation: The verified order r=4 yields factors 3 and 5. The a=14 case has order 2 but only trivial gcds 1 and 15. This traces order finding and factor extraction; it does not execute full Shor.
